dispositions.disposition: Adopted as the reading of overrun step 3, before S7. For a probe <ID>.O<d1...dm>, /targets/<j-1> of its record is candidate d_j, and that target's stop is <ID>.S<d_j>; the Director confirms it by checking that the target's pair.started.path equals candidate d_j's 'after' path, and runs no stop for a target that fails that check. No tool or byte of the freeze changes.

Adopted as the classification reading, before S7. A .P target whose state is 'unknown' only because its pair's records do not exist does not by itself make the outcome UNKNOWN, provided the main command's own records show that the start never happened: for C16 and C19, the runner's NOT_RUN row, or REFUSED_BEFORE_START with PROVEN_ZERO; for C17, a case with no started.json and zero starts in its ledger. The main command's own class then applies, n04's CONTRACT outcome for C19 among them. A target that is 'unknown' for any other reason stays UNKNOWN. S7 stops either way, since that .X is NOT_MET.

Adopted as launch rules, before S7. (a) Order and approval: each launch message holds exactly two calls, the command's first and its timer's second. The session runs in the auto permission mode; so far every Director wrapper call of MH (S5's four, and the reads of S6) started without a prompt. If either call of a launch waits for an approval or is refused, the launch has deviated: a refused or never-started command did not run and S7 stops before it, class HOST (the Director's executor), with no retry; if the command started, the Director waits for its task, runs its .L, its .P where it has one, and its .X as frozen, decides any overrun from the records under (b), and stops S7 after them. (b) Timing: an 'outer-bound' line has effect only if the command's task had not ended when the line was printed, decided from the records: if the wrapper's command record shows end_epoch_s - start_epoch_s not above outer_bound_s, the line had no effect; if the task is still running when the Director reads the line, the overrun procedure begins at once. After an 'exit-file' line, the wrapper's tail (jq, shasum, stat and printf on local files) is unbounded; if its task has not ended when the Director next acts, the Director tells the owner, starts nothing and keeps waiting, as step 6. (c) The tool reports a timer's status 1 as failed; that is the frozen 'outer-bound' result, and the printed line decides.

Recorded, no change. (a) The .P rows' text on an unfrozen stop is superseded by stop rule 4 and overrun step 3: a stop is only <ID>.S<k>, with output <name>.stop-<k>.json; the Director never builds the stale argv. (b) Wrapper exits 91 and 92 come after the exit file is written, so the timer prints 'exit-file' for them; stop rule 11 governs them.
